title: Daily physics — notable papers from the Thu, 5 Nov 2026 arXiv batch
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart. This is an inferred ranking based on sparse same-day citation evidence, limited independent discovery-index signals, concrete results, cross-field relevance, and revisions; it is not a readership or download ranking.

sections.title: Gravitational-Wave Constraints on $R^2$ Gravity
sections.abstract: The authors map quadratic f(R)=R+aR^2 gravity to a one-parameter massive-scalar inspiral waveform and use two binary-neutron-star events to constrain its coupling.
sections.claimed_result: The authors' combined Bayesian analysis of GW170817 and GW190425 gives a≤6.2×10^6 m² at 90% credibility, corresponding to m_s≥3.2×10^-11 eV; the posterior remains consistent with general relativity.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; Bayesian inspiral-waveform analysis of GW170817 and GW190425.
sections.unique_caveat: The modified waveform is developed through 0PN order and the constraint uses only two events; higher-order waveform and neutron-star tidal modeling remain follow-up needs.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: An independent daily gr-qc discovery index places it first among 32 listed papers; it is cross-listed in three physics areas and reports a quantitative gravitational-wave bound. Digest position is only a weak discoverability signal.

sections.title: Experimental activation of hidden metrological steerability in quantum channels via stochastic filtering
sections.abstract: The authors use stochastic pre- and post-filtering to restore a metrological-steering-inequality violation under amplitude damping, demonstrating the effect with photonic polarization qubits.
sections.claimed_result: In the authors' experiment, the damping threshold for violating the metrological steering inequality rises from about 0.5 without filtering to about 0.75 at the strongest tested filter setting.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; heralded single-photon polarization qubits, a two-path Sagnac amplitude-damping channel, and Brewster-angle glass-plate filters.
sections.unique_caveat: The restored advantage is conditional on probabilistic filtering, which reduces event success probability; the demonstration tests amplitude damping rather than arbitrary noise channels.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A separate daily quantum-physics discovery index includes it at position 17; the paper reports a direct photonic test and a quantified change in the noise threshold. Index order is a limited discovery signal, not a popularity statistic.

sections.title: The M87 Black Hole Mass from JWST and Keck Stellar Kinematics Spanning 10 pc to 10 kpc
sections.abstract: The authors combine JWST and Keck stellar-kinematics maps with triaxial orbit modeling to measure M87's central black-hole mass over a wide range of radii.
sections.claimed_result: The authors infer M_BH=(5.38±0.13±0.22)×10^9 M_sun and a mass-to-distance ratio whose 90% credible interval overlaps the multi-epoch EHT result.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; JWST NIRSpec and Keck KCWI stellar kinematics analyzed with triaxial Schwarzschild orbit models.
sections.unique_caveat: The statistical error is smaller than the systematic uncertainty from M87's distance; overlap with the EHT interval compares independent methods and is not a new EHT measurement.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Joins JWST/NIRSpec and Keck/KCWI measurements, fits roughly 5,000 kinematic constraints, and reports an EHT-comparable mass-to-distance interval.

sections.title: Search for GeV-scale axion-like particles in PbPb collisions
sections.abstract: The LHCb Collaboration searches forward PbPb collision data for axion-like particles produced by exclusive photon fusion and decaying to two photons, setting limits in the 3–10 GeV mass range.
sections.claimed_result: Using 0.228 nb^-1 of PbPb data at √s_NN=5.02 TeV, the collaboration probes masses down to 3.0 GeV and couplings down to 3.2×10^-4 GeV^-1, reporting its strongest limits for masses from 3 to 5 GeV.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; LHCb forward detector analysis of PbPb collision data.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper reports search limits, not an axion-like-particle detection; sensitivity is tied to recorded luminosity, forward acceptance, and the assumed exclusive production and decay channel.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A replacement in today's batch and described by the authors as the first forward search for this exclusive photon-fusion channel; provides explicit mass and coupling reach and cross-lists high-energy and nuclear experiment.

sections.title: DESI DR2 Results III: The Mass of the Milky Way
sections.abstract: The DESI Collaboration combines four dynamical models, calibrated on cosmological mock surveys, to infer the Milky Way's mass from 10,036 distant halo stars in DESI DR2.
sections.evidence_type: Observational and computational; DESI DR2 six-dimensional halo-star data, with Gaia DR3-like uncertainties and cosmological mock-survey calibration.
sections.unique_caveat: Corrections depend on mock-based treatment of disequilibrium, selection functions, and differences among dynamical methods and tracers.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A DESI DR2 key-project analysis uses 10,036 halo stars, compares four methods on mocks, and combines method-specific estimates while modeling residual correlations.

sections.title: Near-Quantum-Limited Readout for the Princeton Axion Search using a sub-GHz Kinetic Inductance Traveling Wave Parametric Amplifier
sections.abstract: The authors characterize a kinetic-inductance traveling-wave parametric amplifier operating at 300–700 MHz, reporting gain above 30 dB and system noise of 2.5–3.5 quanta.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report more than 30 dB peak gain and 2.5–3.5 quanta system noise across the stated operating band, with performance meeting the stated Princeton Axion Search requirements.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; TiN kinetic-inductance amplifier characterized with a variable-temperature noise source and readout-chain tests.
sections.unique_caveat: This is amplifier characterization, not an axion detection; measured system noise may include losses between the noise source and amplifier input, and further testing is needed.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in quantum physics, astrophysical instrumentation, and experimental high-energy physics; provides direct gain/noise measurements in a sub-GHz band.

sections.title: New Neutron Polarizabilities from Deuterium Compton Scattering at HI$\gamma$S
sections.abstract: The authors analyze 61 MeV deuterium Compton-scattering measurements at HI$\gamma$S with chiral EFT to extract neutron electric and magnetic scalar polarizabilities.
sections.claimed_result: The authors obtain alpha^n_E1=12.25±1.1(stat)±0.3(BSR)±0.8(th) and beta^n_M1=2.95∓1.1(stat)∓0.3(BSR)∓0.8(th), in units of 10^-4 fm^3.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; circularly polarized 61 MeV gamma beam on liquid deuterium, with NaI(Tl) detectors at three scattering angles, interpreted using chiral EFT.
sections.unique_caveat: The neutron polarizabilities are inferred from a deuteron target through chiral EFT; statistical and theoretical uncertainties remain appreciable.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct cross-section measurements with explicit statistical, Baldin-sum-rule, and theoretical uncertainties; authors report a 12% reduction in statistical uncertainty.

sections.title: Quantum Noise Spectroscopy of Criticality in an Atomically Thin Magnet
sections.abstract: In a v3 revision, the authors use nitrogen-vacancy-center T2 noise magnetometry on trilayer CrSBr to measure critical fluctuations and infer dynamical and correlation-length exponents.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find that the CrSBr transition is Ising-like but deviates from short-range Ising and XY predictions, attributing the difference to long-range dipolar interactions and easy-axis anisotropy.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; NV-center spin-decoherence noise magnetometry on a trilayer CrSBr sample, with model fitting and simulations.
sections.unique_caveat: The universality-class interpretation depends on the noise model and is based on one material and thickness; extension across samples and control parameters is needed.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A substantive v3 replacement appears in today's batch; cross-listed in condensed matter and quantum physics and reports quantitative NV-center noise measurements against criticality models.

sections.title: Hall-Density Collapse as Direct Evidence for Percolative Conduction Onset in Monolayer MoS$_2$ Transistors
authors: C. J. L. de la Rosa
sections.abstract: Temperature-dependent transport and Hall measurements on MoS2 monolayer transistors reveal a Hall-density collapse and vanishing activation energy at a carrier density the authors identify as a percolation threshold.
sections.claimed_result: The authors attribute conduction onset to classical percolation driven by dielectric-interface disorder rather than channel quality alone and report activation barriers above room-temperature thermal energies.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; temperature-dependent transport and Hall measurements in MoS2 FETs with amorphous HfO2 dielectrics.
sections.unique_caveat: The percolation interpretation is tied to the studied device and dielectric interface; journal submission does not mean the preprint is peer-reviewed.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Combines two complementary transport signatures, studies industry-relevant monolayer FETs, and is marked as submitted to Physical Review Letters.

sections.title: Simulating a chiral gauge theory
sections.abstract: The authors construct a gauge-invariant 1+1-dimensional Abelian chiral-gauge lattice model with finite-dimensional qudits and use infinite matrix-product states to reproduce the canonical 34-50 model's infrared behavior.
sections.claimed_result: For the 1+1D Abelian 34-50 model, the authors report that an N=6 finite-dimensional local Hilbert space reproduces expected continuum infrared physics in their infinite-MPS simulation.
sections.evidence_type: Computational and theoretical; Hamiltonian lattice construction with Z_N gauge fields and infinite matrix-product-state simulation.
sections.unique_caveat: The demonstrated result is for a specific 1+1D Abelian model and finite N; it does not establish a general non-Abelian or higher-dimensional construction.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in lattice high-energy theory, condensed matter, and high-energy theory; preserves lattice chiral symmetry/anomaly and compares a nonperturbative simulation with analytic predictions.
